### Jio IPO Day 3 Live: Issue Subscribed 22 Times On Final Day

Jio Platforms Ltd's IPO was subscribed 22.19 times by Day 3, drawing bids for more than 438 crore shares against the 19.75 crore shares on offer, according to NSE data. Heavy demand was driven primarily by Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), whose category was oversubscribed 70.55 times (345 crore bids vs. 4.9 crore shares reserved). Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) followed with a 14-fold subscription (51 crore shares bid), while the Retail Individual Investor (RII) portion saw steady interest, closing at 2.72 times (23.11 crore bids against 8.5 crore shares).

Jio Platforms Ltd's IPO was subscribed 21.03 times by Day 3, drawing bids for more than 415 crore shares against the 19.75 crore shares on offer, according to NSE data. Jio IPO Day 3 Live: Recap

At the end of day one, Jio Platforms Ltd's initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed 5.57 times, with investors bidding for 110.03 crore shares against 19.75 crore shares on offer, according to stock exchange data.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, with their portion subscribed 13.29 times. They bid for 651.46 crore shares against 49.01 crore shares reserved for the category.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed their portion 5.97 times, bidding for 217.58 crore shares against 36.44 crore shares on offer. Within the category, bids above Rs 10 lakh were 6.76 times subscribed, while the Rs 2 lakh-to-Rs 10 lakh segment was subscribed 4.38 times.

The retail individual investor portion was subscribed 1.54 times, with bids for 131.06 crore shares against 85.04 crore shares reserved. Total retail demand crossed Rs 14,650 crore.

The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while bids excluding the anchor book crossed ₹4.9lakh crore. items.title: Jio Platforms IPO turns largest subscribed issue; investors ...
items.author: Gowri Lakshmi
items.text:
Jio ... set the world record for having received more than one crore applications ... being the fastest subscribed IPO ... The telecom giant’s issue was fully subscribed in 100 minutes on the opening day.

...

Jio Platforms Ltd.’s ₹30,213 crore ($3.2 billion) initial public offering closed on Friday with a total demand of more than ₹7 lakh crore. Investors bid for over 20.5 times the issue, making it the highest-value bid in India. The IPO also set the world record to have received more than one crore applications and the fastest subscribed IPO. The telecom giant’s issue was fully subscribed in 100 minutes on the first day.

...

The company has allotted shares worth ₹8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at the upper end of its price band. Institutional demand for the issue reached over ₹2.5 lakh crore, accounting for more than 30 times the available shares. 

Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB), who typically wait till the last day, bid nearly 71 times or 314 crores shares against 4.9 crore shares offered on the last day. Retail investors, who fully subscribed by the second day, offered bids worth 22.8 crore shares against 22.35 crore shares offered on Friday. The retail investors subscribed nearly 2.7 times the issue, signally increased investor sentiment toward large conglomerate listing and telecom and AI stocks. The company is expected to get listed on the exchanges on October 28, Wednesday.

---
